summary: The candidate counters pay a modest amount above the offer, then stays quiet to let the employer answer.
realLife: Campus career advice says to counter about 10 to 20 percent higher if pay is below average for the area, and 5 to 10 percent if it is at or above average, then stay silent so the employer responds first.
sources: UW-Madison SuccessWorks, accepting and negotiating your offer: https://successworks.wisc.edu/accepting-and-negotiating-your-offer/
inGame: Pay in the job record (employer, position, workplace, pay, tenure) in the jobs module; the counter would move pay on a new job record. Needs: an offer negotiation step. Scene: needs a producer for job-offer.

turns.summary: The candidate accepts the first number without countering.
turns.writesBack: The job record starts at the offered pay, with a note of doubt later.

turns.summary: The candidate asks for far more than the offer and the employer pulls back.
pulledBy: an employer with a tight budget
turns.writesBack: The offer is withdrawn or the tie cools, and the job is lost.

turns.summary: The employer meets the candidate partway, with a smaller raise or an extra day of leave.
pulledBy: a record of the pay figure
turns.writesBack: The job record starts at a middle pay, and the hiring manager tie warms.
